item.title: Constitutional Review Commission to submit final report to President today
item.description: The Constitutional Review Commission will submit its final report on the review of the 2013 Constitution to President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu today, marking a major milestone in the six-month review process. The submission follows the completion of the Commission's six-month review.
item.content:encoded:
The Constitutional Review Commission will submit its final report on the review of the 2013 Constitution to President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu today, marking a major milestone in the six-month review process.

The submission follows the completion of the Commission's six-month review.

The Commission says the final report reflects the views, concerns and aspirations shared by Fijians during the public consultation process.

item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Barisal, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: 41-year-old man charged with possession of illicit drugs in Dokanaisuva
item.description: A 41-year-old man has been charged with possession of illicit drugs following a search of his vehicle at a Police checkpoint in Dokanaisuva, Tacirua Heights in Suva. The man and his 35-year-old wife were stopped at the checkpoint at around 1am on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
A 41-year-old man has been charged with possession of illicit drugs following a search of his vehicle at a Police checkpoint in Dokanaisuva, Tacirua Heights in Suva.

The man and his 35-year-old wife were stopped at the checkpoint at around 1am on Saturday.

Police had earlier said officers searched the vehicle and allegedly found white powder believed to be illicit drugs and burglary tools.

They had also said the vehicle had an expired wheel tax, while the 41-year-old man, who was driving, did not have a valid driver's licence.

The 41-year-old will appear in the Suva Magistrates Court today.

item.title: Police increase community engagement with focus on children during school holidays
item.description: Police officers will increase their engagement with communities around the country this week, with a particular focus on keeping children safe during the school holidays. Police say officers will continue visiting communities and talking to people about staying safe and keeping their homes and surroundings secure.
item.content:encoded:
Police officers will increase their engagement with communities around the country this week, with a particular focus on keeping children safe during the school holidays.

Police say officers will continue visiting communities and talking to people about staying safe and keeping their homes and surroundings secure.

Parents and guardians are also being encouraged to regularly talk to their children and keep them occupied with holiday assignments and household chores while they are at home.

The community visits come as the National Federation Party calls for increased Police visibility following concerns about robberies, burglaries and attacks on taxi drivers.

NFP President Parmod Chand has called on Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu to increase patrols and targeted operations in areas affected by crime.

Police are also reminding people that they can call 1681 if they need assistance.

item.title: Nadarivatu Blue-light camp helps young people build skills for life
item.description: Young people who took part in the Nadarivatu Blue-light camp are being encouraged to take the skills and values they learnt back to their homes, schools and communities after completing the week-long programme. Deputy Divisional Police Commander West, Superintendent of Police Esira Bari says the camp was not only about activities and having fun, but also about helping participants develop into res
item.content:encoded:
Young people who took part in the Nadarivatu Blue-light camp are being encouraged to take the skills and values they learnt back to their homes, schools and communities after completing the week-long programme.

Deputy Divisional Police Commander West, Superintendent of Police Esira Bari says the camp was not only about activities and having fun, but also about helping participants develop into responsible and confident young people.

Bari says participants were taught important values including respect, discipline, responsibility, teamwork, resilience, confidence and leadership.

He says the real value of the camp will be seen in how participants apply these lessons in their everyday lives.

Bari encouraged the young people to practise what they learnt and reminded them that the decisions they make will help shape their future.

He also urged parents to continue supporting their children after the camp by listening to them, asking about their experiences and encouraging them to put the lessons they learnt into practice.

Bari says parents should recognise that their children are returning home with new experiences, skills and lessons that can help them grow.

The camp was organised through Fiji Police Community Policing in partnership with Blue Light Fiji, Blue Light New Zealand and other partners.
